newsitem.title: UK: Thorn plunges after profits warning.
newsitem.headline: Thorn plunges after profits warning.

text.p: Shares in Thorn Plc slumped 27p to 224-1/2p after the company said its fourth quarter results would be cut by around 10 percent due to the strength of sterling. The group also said full-year profits before tax and exceptionals would be broadly unchanged from last year's pro forma equivalent of 170.7 million stg.

"The market has not digested this too well. The company didn't have a great Christmas and the problem with sterling is not going to go away anytime soon," the head of trading at a major investment bank said.

The electrical retailer and rental firm, which separated from its music partner EMI in August 1996, said that new business levels were mixed over the third quarter across its main markets in the U.S., the UK and the Nordic region.
One analyst at a major U.S. investment bank in London said sterling was not the major issue for Thorn now.
"There are three factors effecting Thorn: Operating profit in the U.S., U.S. litigation and the introduction of premium tax on insurance in the UK this April."
The analyst, who wished to remain anonymous, expected the share to remain under pressure in the near-term.
"It's a bottomless pit, especially with the U.S. litigation coming up. People should be, and I think are, selling now."
